calls.head: Heavyweight bout
calls.body: The Panthers are near the top of the league for the power play, but the Hurricanes are near the top at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Panthers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. Carolina has had one of the league’s best penalty kills for years, though.

CAR.head: We gave Carolina a 68% chance, but Florida had other ideas.

FLA.head: We gave Florida only a 32% chance, and they proved us wrong.

surprises.head: Florida brought the hits
surprises.body: Florida is one of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams. Even by those standards, this was a lot of hitting: a hit score of 257 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 122 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 600 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: Florida flipped the shot count
surprises.body: Carolina controls the shot count like almost no one else. Not tonight: Florida took 28 of the 44 shot attempts at 5-on-5. From how these two usually play, Florida would expect about 42%. A team strays this far about once every 900 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Markström shuts out the Hurricanes
paras: Bokondji Imama and Nicolas Deslauriers dropped the gloves late in the first. Gustav Forsling scored the only goal of the game in overtime.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Jacob Markström turned aside all 15 shots for the Panthers, and Brandon Bussi stopped 19 of 20.

Neither power play scored: the Panthers killed all six Hurricanes power plays, and the Hurricanes killed all seven of Florida’s. The Cats killed off a two-man advantage that lasted less than two minutes midway through the second. The Panthers improved to 1-0-0, and the Hurricanes fell to 0-0-1.

items.text: It was the first game of the season for both teams, and the Hurricanes lost their home opener.
One of the preview’s three calls held.
